notes: Counts refer to the 72 first-pass sentences (section sentences, FAQ answers, keyFacts values). Added replacement sentences c73-c76 are supported. Search summaries blend pages so attributions are to the page whose title matched the query; the 'every six months' monitoring claim was reported by one summary and denied by another, so the number was dropped. Contradictions with the EXISTING page entry (not edited): (1) seekCare gives 'rapid weight gain (more than 2 kg in three days)': that threshold was not retrieved in any NHS/NHLBI text (NHS says only 'sudden weight gain'); also seekCare says 'seek urgent help' without naming 999 vs NHS 111/same-day GP, and lists 'pink frothy sputum, chest pain, fainting' without routes. (2) overview/definition: 'syndrome ... or can do so only at raised filling pressures', 'Coronary artery disease is the commonest cause', and the listed risk of cocaine use, heart tumours and congenital disease were not retrieved in this pass; unsupported here, not shown contradicted. (3) overview says 'There is no cure'; NHS says no cure for most people (a cure may be possible with a treatable cause such as faulty valves, per one NHS-affiliated summary). (4) treatment text 'rarely, transplantation' and 'ACE inhibitors or ARNI, beta blockers, mineralocorticoid antagonists and SGLT2 inhibitors prolong life' not retrieved as worded (NHS names ACE inhibitors, beta blockers, diuretics, SGLT2 inhibitors only). (5) 'Pitting ankle oedema', 'Third heart sound', 'Raised JVP' signs and 'Enlarged liver' not retrieved. (6) diagnosis states 'BNP is raised' without NT-proBNP/NICE nuance; the draft also wrongly attributed 'lifelong treatment' to NHLBI and had said alcohol 'very little' whereas NHS says drinking within limits is usually possible.
